A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same synthetic propositional-logic and transformer-circuit study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite v4's new title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original transformer-training results, linear-probing experiments, activation interventions, and circuit-sufficiency results for Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-9B, including appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original training and circuit-analysis results and adds further Gemma-2-9B experiments, circuit-reuse tests, and Gemma-2-27B analyses.

M1.justification: The attention-only learner, training objectives, linear probing, and core necessity/sufficiency activation-patching framework are retained. Newly identified logical-operator heads are findings about an existing model; the additional interventions extend the experimental analysis rather than modify a proposed model or algorithm.

E1.justification: Pretrained-LLM evaluation expands from v3's restricted OR problems to the full AND/OR problem for Gemma-2-27B. v4 also investigates later rule-invocation tokens in proofs. These extend test scenarios within the existing synthetic logic domain; the earlier small-transformer study already covered both logical operators.

E2.justification: No competing circuit-discovery method is added or removed. The matched sufficiency comparisons retain the null circuit, full circuit, and four family-removal controls. Gemma-2-27B is an additional subject of mechanistic analysis rather than a baseline against a proposed algorithm.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce the 27B model setting, later proof-token intervention contexts, and targeted path/direct-effect tests. Appendix B.9 fixes mixed true/false premises and queries the logical-operator chain while flipping AND/OR. Existing small-model training budgets and Mistral/Gemma-2-9B six-/four-shot settings are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds Gemma-2-9B rule-location and fact-value interventions, subcircuit-reuse tests for Gemma-2-9B and Mistral-7B, and Gemma-2-27B logical-operator and information-path analyses (Sections 3.3–3.4 and Appendix B.8.4–B.9). Earlier Mistral rule/fact interventions and small-transformer probes remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain standard-deviation reporting, three training seeds for the small transformer, and three repetitions of its operator-flipping intervention. The default 60-sample intervention setting and 200-sample Mistral rule-location experiment are also unchanged. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: v4 adds function-specific Gemma results, proof-stage circuit reuse, and logical-operator/direct-effect findings (Figures 5 and 21–25). Section 3 newly reports 86% accuracy for Gemma-2-27B on the full problem, not a same-setting improvement over OR-only models. Matched sufficiency ratios remain 0.98 for Mistral and 0.94 for Gemma-2-9B: v3 Tables 1–2 correspond to v4 Tables 2–3.

T1.justification: The transformer equations and calibrated-logit metric are retained despite relocation and renumbering. v4's direct/indirect-effect discussion and causal diagram explain the existing intervention framework; they do not introduce a new theorem, proof, or substantively changed mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: v3 foregrounds two contributions: small-transformer routing mechanisms and similar reasoning circuits in two LLMs. v4 centers three-model reasoning circuits and adds headline claims about lazy reasoning, subcircuit reuse, and scale-dependent mechanical differences, including logical-operator heads in Gemma-2-27B.

C2.justification: v4 develops the contrast between intermingled small-model reasoning and lazy, modular LLM reasoning, and interprets the 27B circuit as more parallel than the 9B circuit. It qualifies cross-model similarity and adds specific limitations concerning embedding-level validation, longer reasoning chains, and separating model-size effects from model-family effects.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly documents Gemma-2-9B's sharing of key/value activations between two heads (Section 3.3), while replacing v3 Appendix C.1's complete six-shot prompt with a shorter sampling description in B.1. Small-transformer hyperparameters, optimizer, V100 hardware, and training-time information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion expands substantially to arithmetic, syllogistic reasoning, chain-of-thought mechanisms, and recent reasoning models. Added references include Stolfo et al., Kim et al., Dutta et al., and Pearl. v4 also explicitly positions its scale-dependent findings as a qualification of Tigges et al.'s circuit-consistency results.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves to Section 4, Gemma-2-9B replaces Mistral as the main worked example, and the small-transformer analysis moves from the main text to Appendices C–D. A new appendix outline guides the reorganized material.

P2.justification: v4 introduces an integrated overview and a causal diagram, changes the main circuit illustration to Gemma-2-9B, combines attention statistics into summary panels, and adds intervention, reuse, and path-analysis figures. Earlier plots and tables are extensively relocated; the Gemma sufficiency table is also redisplayed in the main text.

improvement.justification: Additional rule- and fact-specific interventions strengthen Gemma-2-9B's functional interpretation beyond v3's existing QUERY-based and sufficiency evidence. Circuit-reuse tests, clearer exposition, and qualified cross-scale interpretations add value. The gain is limited by the partial 27B investigation, differing task coverage, and reporting ambiguities such as Figure 21 naming Gemma-2-27B inside the Gemma-2-9B analysis.
